title: Samuel Comes to Zarahemla
summary: Samuel the Lamanite comes to Zarahemla, preaches repentance for many days, is cast out, and is about to return to his own land.

explicit_facts.text: In the eighty and sixth year, the Nephites remain in great wickedness while the Lamanites strictly observe the commandments of God according to the law of Moses.
Samuel the Lamanite comes into the land of Zarahemla, preaches repentance for many days, is cast out, and is about to return to his own land.

unspecified_visual_details: Samuel's clothing and appearance; the exact location of his preaching; the people’s individual identities.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict or specify the content of Samuel’s earlier preaching beyond repentance.

title: The Voice Sends Samuel Back

explicit_facts.text: The voice of the Lord comes to Samuel and tells him to return and prophesy whatever comes into his heart.

explicit_facts.text: The people will not let Samuel enter the city; he gets onto its wall, stretches forth his hand, and cries with a loud voice, prophesying to them.

title: The Warning of Justice
summary: Samuel declares the Lord’s words: destruction awaits unless the people repent and have faith in Jesus Christ; he says an angel declared the glad tidings to him and that the people would not receive him.

explicit_facts.text: Samuel says the sword of justice will fall upon the people before four hundred years pass.
Samuel says destruction will come unless the people repent and have faith in Jesus Christ, who will come into the world, suffer many things, and be slain for his people.
Samuel says an angel of the Lord declared glad tidings to him, and that the people would not receive him.

title: The Lord’s Warning to the Nephites
summary: The Lord warns of consequences if the Nephites do not repent and promises to turn away his anger if they do.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says that unless the Nephites repent, he will take away his word, withdraw his Spirit, suffer them no longer, and turn their brethren’s hearts against them.
The Lord says they will be smitten before four hundred years pass, with sword, famine, and pestilence.
The Lord warns that people of the fourth generation among their enemies will behold their destruction unless they repent.
The Lord says he will turn away his anger if they repent and return to him; he blesses those who repent and pronounces woe on those who do not.

explicit_facts.text: Samuel says many in Zarahemla will harden their hearts against the Lord.
The Lord would cause fire to come down from heaven and destroy the city if not for the righteous there, and will spare those who repent.

title: The Curse on Hidden Treasures
summary: Samuel warns that hidden treasures will not be found again unless hidden unto the Lord, and says people will hide treasures when fleeing enemies because their hearts are set on riches.

explicit_facts.text: Those who hide treasures in the earth will not find them again, except a righteous person who hides them unto the Lord.
The Lord says treasures hidden otherwise are cursed and cannot be redeemed because of the curse of the land.
Samuel says people will hide treasures while fleeing enemies because they have set their hearts upon riches, and will be smitten.

title: Riches and Pride

explicit_facts.text: Samuel says the people and their riches are cursed because they set their hearts on riches and do not heed God’s words.

title: The Prophets Cast Out
summary: Samuel condemns the people's mistreatment of prophets, quotes their claim that they would not have persecuted prophets in their fathers' days, and describes how they would respond to a prophet who testified of their sins.

explicit_facts.text: Samuel condemns the people for casting out, mocking, stoning, slaying, and otherwise mistreating prophets.
Samuel quotes the people's claim that they would not have slain, stoned, or cast out prophets in their fathers' days.
Samuel says that if a prophet testified of their sins, the people would become angry, cast him out, and seek to destroy him.
Samuel says the people would call such a prophet false, a sinner, and of the devil.

The foretold lament regrets not repenting when the word of the Lord came and says the land is cursed and all things have become slippery.
